what_its_for: Baclofen is a muscle relaxer used to treat muscle spasms, stiffness, and pain. It is commonly used for conditions like multiple sclerosis (MS), spinal cord injuries, or other conditions that cause tight or spastic muscles. It works by calming the nerves in your spinal cord that cause muscles to tighten up.
how_to_take: Take baclofen exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first — stopping too quickly can cause serious withdrawal symptoms like seizures, confusion, or hallucinations. Your doctor will slowly lower your dose before stopping.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 5 mg taken 3 times a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose every 3 days until your muscles feel better. The typical dose ranges from 40 mg to 80 mg per day, divided into 3 or 4 doses. Do not take more than 80 mg in one day unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Always follow your doctor's personal instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. If you miss several doses in a row, call your doctor for guidance.
storage: Store baclofen tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking baclofen — it can increase dizziness, drowsiness, and the risk of serious side effects. Do not drive a car, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert until you know how baclofen affects you, because it can cause drowsiness or dizziness. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this can cause dizziness or fainting. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially sleeping pills, anxiety medicines, opioid pain medicines, or any other muscle relaxers, as combining these can be dangerous.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe confusion or hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), seizures, severe weakness or trouble breathing, a high fever with stiff muscles and sweating, fainting or extreme dizziness, difficulty urinating or blood in your urine, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if your muscle spasms are not getting better or are getting worse.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your muscle spasms within a few days of starting baclofen, but it often takes 1 to 2 weeks to feel the full benefit. Your doctor will gradually increase your dose to find the amount that works best for you with the fewest side effects. Be patient and do not adjust your dose on your own.
special_populations: Older adults (seniors): Older patients may be more sensitive to baclofen's side effects, especially dizziness, confusion, and falls. A lower starting dose is often used. Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease, your doctor may give you a lower dose because baclofen is removed from your body through the kidneys. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Baclofen may pass into breast milk and is generally not recommended during breastfeeding unless your doctor decides the benefit outweighs the risk. Children: Baclofen is sometimes used in children but only under close supervision of a doctor who will carefully choose the right dose based on the child's weight and condition.
